label: Constructed sample bank
notice: Constructed sample questions written by the project team for tests and the no-API demo. They are not exam or olympiad questions, and their keys were set by the authors.

documents.attribution: Written by the SIMCC capstone team for testing this prototype.

questions.stem: Siti connects each object below, one at a time, into a circuit with a battery and a bulb. Which object makes the bulb light up?
questions.explanation: Steel is a metal. Metals are electrical conductors, so the circuit is closed and the bulb lights up.
questions.subject: Science

topics.evidence: Tests whether an object completes a circuit.

outcomes.evidence: Identify a conductor among common objects.

questions.stem: A battery, a bulb and a switch are connected in one loop. All the parts work, but the bulb does not light up. What is the most likely reason?

options.B: The battery is connected the wrong way round.
options.C: The wires are made of copper.

questions.explanation: An open switch leaves a gap in the circuit, so no current flows and the bulb stays off.
questions.subject: Science

outcomes.evidence: A circuit must be closed for current to flow.

questions.stem: Two identical bulbs are connected in series with one battery. A third identical bulb is then added in series. What happens to the first two bulbs?
questions.explanation: More bulbs in series make the current in the loop smaller, so every bulb is dimmer.
questions.subject: Science

topics.evidence: Effect of adding a bulb in series.

outcomes.evidence: Number of bulbs arranged in series.

questions.stem: The diagram shows a circuit with three identical bulbs, A, B and C, and a switch S1. Switch S1 is open. Which bulbs light up?
questions.explanation: Bulb A is in the same branch as the open switch, so no current passes through it. Bulb B's branch is still closed, and bulb C carries the current to both branches.
questions.subject: Science

topics.evidence: Reads a circuit with a parallel section.

outcomes.evidence: Which loops are closed when S1 is open.

assets.note: Constructed circuit; the server solves it to check the key.

questions.stem: Which part of a simple circuit is its energy source?
questions.explanation: The battery supplies the energy that the other parts of the circuit use.
questions.subject: Science

topics.evidence: Names the parts of a circuit.

outcomes.evidence: The battery is the energy source of the system.

questions.stem: Ali lights a bulb with two batteries connected in series. He then takes out one battery and joins the wires again. How does the bulb change?
questions.explanation: Fewer batteries in series give a smaller current, so the bulb is dimmer but still lights.
questions.subject: Science

outcomes.evidence: Number of batteries arranged in series.

questions.stem: Which object will a magnet attract?
questions.explanation: Magnets attract iron and steel. Copper, glass and plastic are not magnetic.
questions.subject: Science

questions.stem: On a hot day, water droplets form on the outside of a glass of iced water. Where does this water come from?

options.A: Water vapour in the air condenses on the cold glass.
options.B: Water seeps out through the glass.
options.C: The ice melts through the glass.
options.D: The glass releases water when it is cold.

questions.explanation: Water vapour in the surrounding air loses heat to the cold glass and condenses into droplets.
questions.subject: Science

questions.stem: In a plant, which tubes carry water from the roots to the leaves?
questions.explanation: Written in the style of overseas olympiad papers. The 2023 syllabus does not require the terms xylem and phloem, so the bank flags it.
questions.subject: Science
